summary: Hisayoshi Miyamoto works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, and studied under Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi. He held a professorship at Toyo University and posts at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, International Institute for Buddhist Studies, and Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.
Hitoshi Inui is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kanjin Horiuchi. He held appointments at Koyasan University as a lecturer (attested 1986–1992) and as a professor (attested 2015).

Hitoshi Kato is a Buddhist studies scholar. In 1992, he was a part-time lecturer at Osaka University of Foreign Studies and Nara University of Education, and a research assistant at Otani University. In 2016, an affiliation with Osaka University is attested.

Hjalmar Frisk was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Gothenburg. He taught Sanskrit and comparative Indo-European at Lund University in 1937, and served as professor of comparative Indo-European linguistics and Sanskrit at Gothenburg (1938–1967).

Hla Pe was a scholar of linguistics who studied at the University of Rangoon and the University of London. He taught Burmese language and culture at SOAS University of London starting in 1948 and served as Professor of Burmese from 1966 to 1980.
Ho-chin Yang is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Washington by 1994, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp.
Hogen Bays works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under traditional teacher Shodo Harada and served as co-abbot at Great Vow Zen Monastery.
Hoin Yamada is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Ryukoku University around 1959–1963 and was a disciple of Gyōin Hashimoto.
Hoju is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Peking University from around 1999 to 2005 and at KU Leuven from around 2005 to 2007. He taught Kyokuga Saeki.

Hoju Shioda is a Buddhist studies scholar affiliated with Minobusan University as an assistant professor and vice-director (attested 2026). Additional posts attested in 2026 include part-time lecturer roles at Doho University, Daido University Graduate School, and Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Hojun Nagasaki is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara. He was a professor at Otani University (~1970–1999) and served as president of the Japan Association of Jain Studies in 1998.
Hokai was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hogetsu and Zuihe.
Hokei Izumi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Otani University and under Bunyiu Nanjio. He held a professorship at Otani University (attested 1930).
Hoko Kuwana is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (attested 2015). He holds a post as director at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

Holden Furber was a historian and Indologist who studied at Harvard and Oxford. He served as a lecturer at Harvard (~1930–1936), taught history at the University of Texas at Austin (1940–1948), and was professor of South Asia Studies at Penn (1948–1973).

Holger Pedersen was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Copenhagen, Leipzig, Berlin, and Greifswald. He succeeded Vilhelm Thomsen at the University of Copenhagen in 1912, having served there as privatdozent (1897) and extraordinary professor (1903).

Holly Gayley is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied Tibetan and Himalayan Studies at Harvard University (~2000–2009) and held a post at the University of Colorado Boulder around 2008.

Holmes Welch was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who earned his BA and MA at Harvard University. He served as a lecturer at Yale University and at Harvard University (~1963–1981).

Hong Luo is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Peking University in 2007. He worked at the China Tibetology Research Center (2007–2017), became professor at Sichuan University in 2018, and was a research fellow at Hamburg.

Hongyue Guo is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Xubang Qi and earned her PhD at Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2007) under the supervision of Stephen R. Bokenkamp.
